p4.title: Cats
p4.text: Cats are small animals __(0)__ live with people in their homes. A cat can sleep __(1)__ sixteen hours a day! Cats like __(2)__ warm places, like a chair next to a window. They wash themselves with their tongues, so they are __(3)__ clean. Cats can see very well at night and they can jump very __(4)__. Many children __(5)__ got a cat at home. Cats are very good friends.

parts.text: It was Grandma's birthday. Sally and her dad wanted to make a cake for her. Dad found the eggs, the flour and the sugar, and Sally found a big bowl. 'Let's make a chocolate cake,' said Sally. 'It's Grandma's favourite.'

p1.scene: Two pictures of the same living room. Left: the examiner's picture. Right: your picture.
p1.examiner: Look at the two pictures. Here the cat is sleeping on the sofa, but here the cat is on the floor. What other differences can you see?
differences: In your picture the girl is reading a book, but in my picture she is watching TV.
In your picture there are three cushions on the sofa, but in my picture there are two.
In your picture the lamp is on, but in my picture it is off.
In your picture the window is open, but in my picture it is closed.
In your picture there is a plant next to the door, but in my picture there is a chair.

p2.title: Vicky helps at home
p2.examiner_open: These pictures show a story. It's called 'Vicky helps at home'. Look at the pictures first. Vicky's mum is ill in bed. Vicky wants to help, so she goes to the kitchen. Now you tell the story.
frames: Vicky's mum is ill in bed with a cold. Vicky brings her a cup of tea and wants to help.
Vicky goes to the kitchen and starts to wash the dishes, but there is water and soap everywhere!
Vicky's little brother helps her clean the floor. The kitchen is clean again and the dog is happy.
Mum comes to the kitchen and sees the clean room. She hugs Vicky and her brother. Everybody is happy.

sets.reason: A bird isn't in the kitchen. It's an animal.
You don't sit or sleep on an orange. You eat it.
A car isn't a room. You drive it.
You don't clean with a cake. You eat it.

p1: Part One. Look at the picture. Listen and look. There is one example.
Look at this photo, Grandpa. It's our house on Saturday morning. Everybody is helping.
Who's the girl washing the dishes?
That's my cousin Julia. She washes them very carefully.
Can you see the line? This is an example. Now you listen and draw lines.
And who's the boy in the garden? He's got a rabbit.
That's Jack. He gives the rabbit its food every morning. Carrots and grass.
Can you see the woman with the brush? She's painting the wall.
Yes. She's painting the wall yellow. It was white before.
Look at that man in the kitchen. What's he cooking?
That's Uncle Fred. He's making soup with a very big spoon. It's vegetable soup.
And that's Sally. She's cleaning the window with a cloth.
The window looks very clean now.
Yes, she cleaned all the windows in the house!
Who's the boy on the stairs? He's carrying a big basket.
That's Tom. The basket is full of clean clothes. He's taking them upstairs.
Now listen to Part One again.
p2: Part Two. Listen and look. There is one example.
Ben, I've got some jobs for you this Saturday. Can you help me?
Yes, Mum. What's the first job?
First, clean the bathroom, please. It's very dirty.
Can you see the answer? Now you listen and write.
Then, Grandma's cat is staying with us this week. Can you look after her?
Pepper. That's a funny name for a cat.
When do I give Pepper her food?
At twelve o'clock. Not before, or she gets fat!
After lunch, can you water the plants?
The plants in the living room?
No, the plants in the garden. It's very hot and they need lots of water.
Then go to the shop and buy some eggs, please. We need twenty.
Yes, I'm making cakes for the school party.
One more thing. The clean clothes are on your bed. Put them in the cupboard, please.
In the cupboard. OK, Mum. Can I play with my friends after that?
Now listen to Part Two again.
p3: Part Three. Listen and look. There is one example.
Daisy is telling her friend what everybody in her family does at home on Saturdays. What does each person do?
Daisy, what do you do at home on Saturdays?
I make all the beds. Mine, my brother's and my parents'. It takes a long time!
Can you see the letter G? Now you listen and write a letter in each box.
He washes the car. He does it every Saturday, so the car is always very clean and it's blue again!
My mum goes to the supermarket. She does the shopping for the whole week. She comes back with lots of bags.
He gives the dog his food and water. The dog loves him because of that! Then they play in the garden.
My grandmother cooks lunch for everybody. She makes fantastic chicken and rice. We all sit at the big table.
I'd like to come to your house!
And your grandfather? Does he cook too?
No! He waters the plants in the garden. He's got hundreds of flowers. He talks to them!
Now listen to Part Three again.
p4: Part Four. Look at the pictures. Listen and look. There is one example.
Mum, where's my coat? Is it in the cupboard?
No, Peter. It's on the chair in the kitchen. You left it there.
Can you see the tick? Now you listen and tick the box.
One. What is Mum going to cook tonight?
Mum, are we having soup tonight?
No, we had soup yesterday. I'm cooking rice with chicken.
Two. What does Grandpa need from the shop?
Sam, can you go to the shop for me? We've got bread and eggs, but there isn't any milk.
Milk. OK, Grandpa. A big bottle?
Three. Which room is Lily cleaning?
Lily, are you cleaning the bathroom?
No, Dad. Mum cleaned the bathroom. I'm cleaning my bedroom. It's very untidy!
Four. What is the dog doing?
Where's the dog? Is he sleeping in the garden?
No, he's in the kitchen. He's eating his dinner.
He played with his ball before.
Sam! What was that noise? Did you break a cup?
No, Mum. Sorry. I broke a plate. It fell off the table.
Oh dear. Is the lamp all right?
Now listen to Part Four again.
p5: Part Five. Look at the picture. Listen and look. There is one example.
Here's a picture of a living room. Can you see the cushion on the sofa?
Can you see the purple cushion? This is an example. Now you listen and colour and write.
Now, can you see the lamp on the small table?
There's a cat on the sofa. Can I colour it?
Grey. Like my cat at home!
Can you see the plant next to the window?
Yes. Shall I colour it green?
Yes. There's a picture on the wall with nothing in it. Write the word 'home' in it. H-O-M-E.
And now the ball under the table. Colour it red, please.
Well done. That's a lovely living room.
Now listen to Part Five again.
